text:
B: Hello. Tomasz, Peterborough.
A: Alright. Liam. Normanton, near Wakefield.
B: Wakefield. Okay.
A: Yeah.
B: You work?
A: Warehouse. Picking. Part-time, four shifts, mostly lates.
B: Part-time. Why part-time? You are young.
A: Leaves my days free, like. I do trainers on the side, reselling. And I'm knackered enough on four, to be honest.
B: Four shifts and knackered. I do forty hours, rotating, early and late. Last night I did night shift. Is normal.
A: Little laugh. Yeah, fair enough. What d'you do?
B: Electrician in a food factory. Team leader. If a line stops, they call me.
A: We've got engineers like that at ours. Everyone goes quiet when they walk past.
B: Good. They should go quiet.
A: Ha. Yeah.
B: You drive forklift?
A: I had the ticket, counterbalance. Work paid. It's lapsed now, though. Keep meaning to book it again, 'cause it's a bit more an hour.
B: So book it. Is one phone call.
A: Yeah. Prob will. Everyone keeps saying that today.
B: Then everyone is right, no?
A: Yeah, suppose.
B: What car you have?
A: Old Golf. Mk6. Keep it clean, mind, it's mint inside. Needs an MOT though, and I'm skint till Friday, so I'm sort of hoping nothing comes up on it.
B: What year?
A: 2010. Done about a hundred and twenty thousand.
B: Check the suspension, the front, the drop links. On Golf this age they always knock. And the brake discs. If you do yourself before MOT, you save a lot. Garage will charge you double for parts and labour, they see young guy, they see money.
A: I can do bulbs and that. Fluids. Never done discs.
B: Is not difficult. YouTube, a jack, two hours. My son did his first one at sixteen with me.
A: Yeah? I did start a mechanics course at college. Level 2. Packed it in after about six months.
B: Why?
A: Dunno. Didn't fancy it at the time. Wish I'd stuck at it now, to be fair, 'cause I'd be on decent money.
B: Is not too late. Thirty?
A: Thirty, yeah.
B: I am forty-eight, I did inspection and testing course at college here, Peterborough, three years ago. In English, which is not my language. You can do level 2 at thirty.
A: Yeah. Maybe. What d'you drive, then?
B: BMW, Five Series. Old one. I just got the alloys off Facebook, he wanted three hundred, I paid one eighty.
A: Nice. That's how I do trainers. Never pay what they ask. If you look keen, you're done.
B: Exactly this. If you look like you want it, you pay too much. Same with cars, same with everything.
A: Do you know what I mean. People just click buy.
B: My daughter is like this. Everything is click, click, it arrives. She wants driving lessons now, thirty-five pound an hour, I say—
